concepts.definition: The Aristotelian soul-power or psychic phenomenon by which a phantasma is presented (DA 428a1-2); whether faculty, phenomenon, or aspect of perception is itself a debate axis.
synonyms_merged: phantasia as the De Anima faculty

concepts.definition: The product or vehicle of phantasia; variously read as inner appearance, mental representation, image-trace, or motion in the central sense organ. Verbal noun of phainesthai.
Sense-perception; reception of sensible form without matter (DA II.12 424a18-19); phantasia's causal source and its closest neighbor faculty.

concepts.canonical_name: phantasia as kinesis caused by aisthesis-in-act
concepts.definition: Aristotle's canonical definition (DA 428b10-15, 429a1-2): phantasia is a motion (kinesis) in the soul that comes to be as a result of perception's actual operation. The decaying-sense substrate.
The verb 'to appear/seem' and its forms (phainesthai, phainetai, phainomena, phainein); the lexical-etymological anchor of the entire phantasia-family.
The rational species (DA 433b29, 434a5-11): combines many phantasmata into one (hen ek pleionon) for choice against a single criterion; peculiar to humans.
The non-rational species shared with animals (DA 433b29-30, 434a6): single momentary appearings without overall plan; the middle tier in Papachristou's scheme.

Aristotle's stylistic strategy (Rhet. 3.10-11; cf. DA 427b18-19, Mem. 450a, Poet. 1455a) by which language renders absent things present to the mind's eye; the principal rhetorical/mnemonic engine of phantasia.

concepts.canonical_name: phantasia/aisthesis identity 'same in capacity, different in being'
concepts.definition: Aristotle's mode of non-identity (DA 433a31, De Insomn. 459a15-18): two powers always co-instantiated may still differ in essence (toi einai); the formula governing phantasia-aisthesis relation.
synonyms_merged: same in capacity / different in einai

concepts.definition: MA 702a18ff., DA 432b15, 433b26-30: phantasia 'prepares' desire (orexis); animal motion is impossible without phantasia. The action-explanation nexus.
MA 700b17ff.: phantasia listed alongside aisthesis and nous as kritika, faculties that judge/discriminate objects under descriptions for the desiring soul.
DA 428a20-24: phantasia does not necessarily carry pistis (conviction); doxa does. Non-rational animals have phantasia but not belief.
DA 428a11-12, 428b17-22: aisthesis is (incidentally) always accurate of its proper object, but phantasia can be false; phantasia most active when perception is indistinct.
DA 432a9-10, 431a14-17: phantasmata are like aisthemata only without matter; they serve as aisthemata to the thinking soul (the storehouse-of-forms function).
synonyms_merged: preserver and storehouse of sensible forms

concepts.canonical_name: thinking is never without a phantasma
concepts.definition: DA III.7-8 (431a14-17, 431b2, 432a3-14): the noetic soul never thinks without a phantasma; the forms thought are 'in' phantasmata; thus phantasia is the substrate-vehicle of intellect.
synonyms_merged: phantasia as bridge between sensible and intelligible
phantasia as basis for higher cognition
phantasia mediates unity of nous and aisthesis

concepts.definition: Aristotle's exclusion at the opening of DA III.3: phantasia is the power 'in virtue of which a phantasma is said to come to be — and not what we call phantasia by transferred sense.'
Rhet. I.11 1370a28-29: phantasia is 'a sort of weak perception,' connected with memory and hope; the working definition in the Rhetoric.
DA 427b17-21: phantasia, unlike doxa, is voluntary — we can set images before our eyes 'whenever we wish.' Connected to mnemonic practice (Simonides).
EN 1114a32, EE 1235b25-29: what appears good depends on the agent's character; the action-theoretic role of phantasia in moral psychology.
Rhet. 1382a21 (fear = phantasia of future evil), 1383a17 (courage), 1384a22 (shame = phantasia of reputation-loss): emotions are constitutively phantasia-engagements.
synonyms_merged: shame as phantasia of reputation loss

concepts.definition: Rhet. 3.11.1411b22-23 + Metaph. 9.5: presence-of-the-thing; in style, depicting subjects as in motion/life (kinesis, zoos); fuels pro ommaton poiein.
Magnitude, amplification, superiority (Rhet. 1.9): rhetoric's scale-rendering operations through which phantasia produces magnitude-bearing images for praise/blame.

Hawhee's umbrella term: the capacity by which words form, conjure, or alter visual perception in audiences; abstracted from Rhet. cluster (phantasia, pro ommaton poiein, energeia, enargeia, megethos, hyperoche, asteia).
Nussbaum's signature gloss (Wittgenstein, Ishiguro): phantasia is the interpretive aspect of perception by which an animal sees an object as F — not internal-picture-inspection.
The traditional reading (Ross, Hicks, Hamlyn, Rees, Freudenthal, Sorabji) that phantasia always involves internal images representing by similarity and inspected by the agent.
White's exegetical move: at 427b21-24 Aristotle separates phantasia from judgment by detachment from immediate affect — phantasia 'coolly regards affecting scenes as one would a picture.'
synonyms_merged: coolly regards scenes as a picture

concepts.canonical_name: causal-powers (not causal-ancestry) account of phantasma content
concepts.definition: Caston's signature formalization: phantasma content is fixed by its causal powers to mimic sensory stimulations, not by its actual causal history — permitting content-cause divergence (salamander-to-dragon case).

Caston: phantasia-content is a non-conceptual, pre-predicative form of intentionality, distinct from the combination-falsehood of Metaph. 9.10 1051b1-6; the basic intentional currency below the conceptual.

concepts.canonical_name: synthesis of the manifold (panoramic field of vision)
concepts.definition: Frede: phantasia performs the synthesis-of-the-manifold that piecemeal sense-perception cannot deliver; supplies the wider 'field of vision' (Kant's house example).
synonyms_merged: no panoramic field of vision in perception

concepts.definition: APo. II.19 99b36-100b9: the aisthesis-to-memory-to-experience-to-nous progression toward first principles consists in phantasiai. Phantasmata as 'standardized pictures' enabling generalization.
synonyms_merged: phantasmata as standardized picture for generalization

concepts.definition: Papachristou's third grade (DA III.11 433b31-434a5): the lowest, sub-sensitive tier in imperfect animals (zoophytes, molluscs) where phantasma does not persist after the sense object.
DA 427b14-16: the cognitive umbrella under which doxa, episteme, and phronesis fall; never occurs without phantasia. Locates phantasia as constitutive of rhetorical krisis-formation.
O'Gorman: epideictic, classified as audience-of-theoros (Rhet. 1358b), is the primal phantasmatic function of public discourse — image-of-scale construction underlying deliberation and judgment.
Rhet. 1404a11 read non-disparagingly (Gonzalez, O'Gorman, Hawhee): style is the rhetorical medium that produces phantasmata in the auditor's psyche; bridges Rhet. III with DA III.3.
Rhet. 3.2, 3.10-11: metaphor that 'sets before the eyes' through energeia-signifying terms; the urbane-wit (asteia) locus where rhetorical vision concentrates.
DA II.8 420b31ff., GA 786b23-25, Pol. 1253a10-11: voice is meaningful only because produced by a creature with phantasia; the sensorial-acoustic channel of rhetorical phantasmata.
DA 428b19, Metaph. 9.10 1051b15-32: sensation of proper perceptibles and conception of incomposites are infallible (or have falsity 'to the least extent'); the bullet Aristotle bites.
MA 701b17-21: phantasia, like aisthesis, has bodily realization; this is why non-perceptual thought can move the body (token-not-type physicalism, on Nussbaum's gloss).
White's signature thesis: phantasia 'lends stability to appearances they do not have of themselves'; provides the temporal substrate (memory of past, projection of future) for nous's timeless object.
synonyms_merged: preserver and storehouse of sensible forms

concepts.definition: Papachristou: calculative phantasmata bear BOTH propositional content (DA III.11 434a7-8) and pictorial content (DA III.7 431b6-8) — prefiguring the Kosslyn-vs-Pylyshyn imagery debate.
White: phantasia arises in the gap between sensing and thinking, between Platonic-Protagorean flux and being; the metaphysical setting of DA III.3.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia-as-interpretation / seeing-as (Nussbaum)
readings.statement: Phantasia is the interpretive aspect of perception — object-as-F awareness, Wittgensteinian seeing-as — not internal-picture inspection.

readings.reading_name: Decaying-sense passages are theoretically isolable (Nussbaum)
readings.statement: The Parva Naturalia decaying-sense material describes a physiological hypothesis about memory/dreams and cannot govern phantasia generally.

readings.reading_name: DA 428a1-4 kata metaphoran brackets 'mere show,' not phainetai (Nussbaum)
readings.statement: Aristotle's kata-metaphoran exclusion targets the post-Herodotean 'ostentation' sense of phantasia, not the ordinary phainetai-uses.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia/aisthesis are one capacity under two descriptions (Nussbaum)
readings.statement: DA 433a31's 'same in capacity different in einai' should be read on the arete/dikaiosune model: one disposition, two descriptions.

readings.reading_name: Deliberative phantasia is inferential, not collage-of-pictures (Nussbaum)
readings.statement: DA 434a7-10's 'one phantasma out of many' means inferential joining of consequences under a single criterion, not a Rossian image-montage.

readings.reading_name: All thought has a concrete symbolic vehicle (Nussbaum)
readings.statement: DA 432a3-10's 'soul never thinks without phantasma' is the empirical thesis that every thought is accompanied by image, formalization, or words.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia as preparation for noein — theoretical-cognitive priority (White)
readings.statement: Phantasia in DA III.3-8 is a preliminary theoretical-cognitive condition for the analysis of nous, not primarily a faculty of practical action.

readings.reading_name: Picture-vs-encounter distinction as litmus (White)
readings.statement: DA 427b21-24 separates phantasia from judgment by detachment from affect: phantasia 'coolly regards' scenes; judgment moves us.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia as temporal mediator and interior landscape (White)
readings.statement: Phantasia preserves sensible forms past the now of aisthesis, providing a stable interior landscape that gives nous a foothold in time.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia supervenes on aisthesis (Frede)
readings.statement: Phantasia is NOT a separate faculty but a phenomenon supervening on sense-perception; the phantastikon is not listed among the soul's faculties.

readings.reading_name: Two functions: synthesis-and-retention + bridging to intellect (Frede)
readings.statement: Phantasia performs (a) synthesis of the manifold/retention, supplying field of vision, and (b) the bridge between intellect and sensible objects.

readings.reading_name: Strict aisthetikon/noeton dualism preserved (Frede)
readings.statement: Phantasia mediates but remains confined to the sensible side; Aristotle denies intellectual memory and refuses any 'real fusion' (anti-Modrak).

readings.reading_name: Phantasia is a unified concept (Frede, against Schofield)
readings.statement: All phantasiai share a uniform causal account as motions in the soul caused by sense-perceptions; pace Schofield's 'loose-knit family.'

readings.reading_name: Functional-explanatory reading: phantasia solves the problem of error (Caston)
readings.statement: Phantasia is introduced in DA 3.3 not to add a special imaging faculty but to solve a structural problem of error inherited by Aristotle's own theory.

readings.reading_name: Causal-powers (not causal-ancestry) account of phantasma content (Caston)
readings.statement: Phantasma content is fixed by causal powers to mimic sensory stimulations, not by causal history — allowing content-cause divergence.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia as non-propositional intentionality (Caston)
readings.statement: Phantasia provides intentional content below the conceptual/predicational threshold; the basic intentional currency of the soul.

readings.reading_name: Epideictic-as-phantasmatic function (O'Gorman)
readings.statement: Phantasia's rhetorical home is the epideictic function (megethos/auxesis), not Book III lexis narrowly; the primal phantasmatic function of public discourse.

readings.reading_name: Rhetorical order parallels psychic order (O'Gorman)
readings.statement: Epideictic is rhetorically 'primal yet foundational' as phantasia is psychically 'lower yet foundational' — inverting the linear-rationalist account of Rhet.

readings.reading_name: Psychological-phantasia thesis: Rhet. 1404a11 = the De Anima faculty (Gonzalez)
readings.statement: The phantasia of Rhet. III.1 1404a11 is the same psychological function described in DA, not 'mere outward show'; the Cope/Freese/Kennedy tradition is wrong.

readings.reading_name: Phantasia-with-pistis is the rhetorical goal (Gonzalez)
readings.statement: The orator's task is to convert phantasia (which lacks pistis) into pistis-bearing phantasia, i.e., into doxa, via lexis-and-pathos.

readings.reading_name: Rhetorical vision: words form direct sensory perception, not just metaphor (Hawhee)
readings.statement: Phantasia in Rhet. operates at or near direct sensory perception, not only at cognitive metaphor; pathē are 'seen through' phantasia in a matrix of phantastic visibility.

readings.reading_name: Three kinds/grades of phantasia (Papachristou)
readings.statement: Against the binary logistike/aisthetike reading, DA III.11 433b31-434a5 (with Aquinas, Themistius, Philoponus) establishes a third indefinite tier in imperfect animals.

merge_notes: kept aisthesis/aisthema separate as PHX-C-003 (umbrella) without spawning a Tier-3 — aisthema folded into definition since no unit treats it as autonomous load-bearing
kept indefinite phantasia (PHX-C-031) separate from perceptual/sensitive (PHX-C-007) because Papachristou's whole thesis turns on the distinction
merged decaying-sense, motus phantasiae, kinesis-definition, and echo-of-sensation into PHX-C-004 — all are surface variants of the same causal-physiological claim
kept image-view (PHX-C-025) and interpretive seeing-as (PHX-C-024) as separate concepts because the debate axis requires them as opposed poles, not as one notion

lexis-as-phantasia (PHX-C-034) absorbs Gonzalez's many fine philological sub-concepts (adverbial kai, hypokrisis-subordination, pros doxan, didaskalia) since they are arguments FOR the same canonical thesis
megethos / hyperoche / auxesis merged into one cluster (PHX-C-022) — they are amplification's coordinated triad in Rhet. 1.9
kept energeia (PHX-C-021) separate from rhetorical vision (PHX-C-023) because energeia is a textual Aristotelian term, rhetorical-vision is Hawhee's umbrella construct
